mechanism_conclusion.phase_scoped_timeout: Time-based cleanup is safe for PREPARED prefixes because they carry no authority. It is unsafe to let time alone revoke GRANTED or AUTHORIZED state.
mechanism_conclusion.task_owned_resume: A rematerialized invocation should resume the same deterministic reservation ID rather than take over with a new worker-owned claim.
mechanism_conclusion.single_grant_record: After full cell acquisition, use one CAS-monotone grant record. GRANTED may transition to exactly one of CANCELLED or AUTHORIZED; if authorization wins, cancellation/replacement must fail closed and reconcile rather than pretending revocation succeeded.
mechanism_conclusion.separate_cancel_is_not_enough: A cancellation flag in a separate authority object can race a worker that already observed GRANTED; without atomic authorization fencing, the tested late-old slice is unsafe.
mechanism_conclusion.authorized_is_absorbing_for_revocation: Once AUTHORIZED is durably minted, replacement must not revoke by lease expiry or late cancellation. Resume/reconcile the same durable effect identity instead.

phase1_assessment.repository_local_cleanup_candidate: PREPARED-only lease cleanup + deterministic same-task resume + single grant-record CAS cancellation/authorization fork is Chat-capable with lightweight repository state/CAS.
phase1_assessment.residual_richer_mode_or_manual_user_exec: none for the tested repository-local state machine
phase1_assessment.external_sink_atomic_participation: unresolved child: after AUTHORIZED, an arbitrary protected/non-idempotent external sink still needs durable effect identity/status or sink-side idempotency/fencing; this is not counted solved.

scope_limit: Three reservation phases, same-task vs replacement, two race orders, repository-atomic vs non-fenced external effect domain. The model assumes PREPARED has no effect authority and GRANTED cancellation/authorization live in one CAS record.
exact_continuation: Cancellation/release atomicity after a GRANT record wins CANCELLED. Compare immediate multi-cell release, lazy tombstoned release, per-cell cancel epoch, reservation-level CANCELLED tombstone checked by all new claimants, and staged integrator. Enumerate partial cell-release crash, response loss, rate-limit interruption, old PREPARED/GRANTED owner return, new claimant acquiring a subset while stale cells remain, cancellation tombstone rollback/GC, and cell delete/recreate ABA. Determine whether one durable reservation-level cancellation tombstone can safely decouple logical revocation from best-effort per-cell cleanup without creating permanent false exclusion or re-admission holes.
